articles.title: AI Is Becoming a Modern Oracle for Tarot Readers—But Should It Be?
articles.summary: A new study reveals tarot practitioners are increasingly using AI to interpret cards, seeking clarity but risking emotional dependence. Researchers interviewed 12 readers who use AI, finding they value its speed but worry it ignores personal context. Nearly 1 in 3 Americans now use tarot or astrology yearly.

articles.title: From Atlanta to Montgomery: A New Generation Rides for Voting Rights
articles.summary: Activists retraced the historic 1965 march route to protest a Supreme Court ruling that struck down a majority-Black district in Louisiana, prompting states like Alabama to redraw maps. Organized by Fair Fight Action, the rally drew diverse attendees, from a 62-year-old grandfather to an 18-year-old organizer, all demanding restored voting protections.

articles.title: Five PMs in Seven Years: Is the UK Becoming Ungovernable?
articles.summary: The UK's rapid turnover of prime ministers—five in seven years—raises questions about governability. Experts blame a mix of global crises, inexperienced leaders, and social media-driven short-termism. While PM Keir Starmer insists the country is governable, he admits frustration with bureaucratic hurdles.
